messages.author: ec32e5a92a275a89
messages.subject: Re: Review Process
parts: I'll respond with my understandings below.

On 04/08/2011 11:39 PM, Ravi Varadhan wrote:
> As I am new to this process, I have a huge number of questions. Here are just a few:
>
> Should everyone vote on all the proposals?
>

I believe all mentors should vote on all projects on which they have some understanding.
If it is really outside your area, then don't vote. If it is not comprehensible, that may
be a reason to vote too, but definitely a reason to comment that it doesn't tell people
why it is worthwhile.

Caveat: We are having some difficulty with Melange in getting some folk on board. We have
even more problems getting them OFF. Unfortunately, the system is very persistent and we
have to ask Google/Melange people to remove some people who are trying to game the system.
> Are the scores blinded or unblinded?

I'm not sure about this. Actually as admin, it is quite important that we know if there
are trolls who have managed to vote. For example, people we thought were mentors but
simply friends of (or even the same person) as the applicant. So as admin, I"m for very
open voting, and encourage attributed comments. I also believe that if folk believe things
are transparent, they back up their vote with solid reasons presented politely.

>
> Should each scorer be asked to provide a brief justification of their scores?
>
My preference. We want to have good proposals that result in good code.

> How is the ranking done - is it the average score or total score?
>

I think total in the past. One thing is clear -- the system is NOT very clear!

From an admin point of view, I really hope we can get a truly fair appraisal of the
projects. For that, we all need to share ideas coherently.

Best

JN

messages.author: 29bcefae00c9a0bb
messages.subject: RE: Review Process
parts:
Thanks, John. I completely agree with all the points. The process should be transparent and that all mentors should try and weigh in on all the proposals to the extent possible. There should be an open discussion after all the scores have been tallied. Mentors should be allowed to re-evaluate their scores on the basis of the discussion so that there is less variance ("shrinkage") in the post-discussion scores than the pre-discussion ones. This approach is used by a number of societies in clinical research for accepting abstracts/manuscripts to special invited symposia. I am not sure if melange would allow us to re-do the scores, but it is worth finding out.

Thanks & Best,
Ravi.
